test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Armature and Coil Winder) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the purpose of measuring electrode resistance during the installation of an earthing system?

options.text: Determining the System's Electrical Load Capacity
Ensuring low impedance in the earthing system for the dissipation of fault current.
Ensuring Proper Grounding of Electrical Equipment

solution:
The correct answer is __Ensuring low impedance in the earthing system for the dissipation of fault current****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Measuring electrode resistance__ is crucial to ensure effective earthing.
 
• It verifies that the earthing system has low impedance to safely dissipate fault currents.
 
• Low resistance in the earthing system minimizes risks to equipment and personnel in case of electrical faults.
 
• Regular testing ensures consistent performance of the earthing system over time.
 
• This process helps prevent voltage build-up that could damage equipment or pose safety risks.
 
• It is a standard practice in electrical installations to maintain safety and system integrity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrical Load Capacity:**
 
 
• This refers to the total amount of electrical load a system can handle without failure.
 
• It is unrelated to measuring electrode resistance during earthing system installation.
 
 
 
• **Insulation Resistance Testing:**
 
 
• This is used to measure the resistance of electrical insulation, ensuring there are no leaks or faults.
 
• It does not serve the purpose of verifying earthing system impedance.
